receipt: P1.11 independent verification of the 47 MOB-recon recoveries
status: INDEPENDENT - derived by a different data path from the resolver
independence_method: Independence was achieved by deriving the chromosome/plasmid assignment from a DIFFERENT data path than the frozen parser. I first read /work/p112/env/run/parsers.py::parse_mobsuite (lines 46-54) and established that it treats exactly ONE file as mandatory - mob/contig_report.txt - requiring the columns contig_id and molecule_type, deriving each call from the molecule_type cell, raising ParseError on any value outside {plasmid,chromosome}, and filling every assembly contig absent from the table with 'unknown'. My own checker (written to /tmp/vv_indep_check.py on the host, run, then deleted) never calls that function for its derivation. It rebuilds the assembly universe by MEASURING sequence lengths in assemblies/shortread/<sample>/shortread.fasta (header 'length=' tokens are not trusted), then derives every call purely from FASTA record membership in mob/chromosome.fasta and mob/plasmid_*.fasta: a contig whose record sits in a plasmid_*.fasta is plasmid, in chromosome.fasta is chromosome, in neither is unknown. contig_report.txt is used only for independent schema validation and as a cross-check target, never as the source of my calls. On top of that I ran my own required-file-set rule (contig_report.txt, chromosome.fasta, mge.report.txt, biomarkers.blast.txt, plus mobtyper_results.txt whenever any plasmid FASTA exists, plus absence of a leftover mob/__tmp working directory), my own schema validation (exact 24-column mob_recon header, per-row field count, molecule_type domain, integer size, gc in [0,1], 32-hex md5, no duplicate contig_id, mobtyper row count equal to plasmid FASTA count), and my own reconciliation (contig-id set equality in both directions between contig_report, the output FASTAs and the assembly, plus per-contig length agreement between reported size, measured output-FASTA sequence length and measured assembly sequence length). Only after all 47 verdicts were fixed did I import the frozen parser as a THIRD opinion and diff it against mine. Three derivations agree: FASTA membership (mine), the molecule_type column (mine, independently read), and parse_mobsuite (frozen) - 0 disagreeing contigs out of 11,241. I also ran the same checker over the 30 mobsuite units that already had status=OK as a positive control (0 problems, 0 diffs) and over the 2 genuine .failed units as a negative control.
notes: INDEPENDENT DETERMINATION OF THE COHORT: I enumerated the 79 mobsuite units myself from inference/state and inference/receipts without consulting the resolver's list. Markers: 77 .done, 2 .failed; every sample has EXACTLY ONE terminal marker (no sample carries both). Receipt statuses: 30 OK/0, 47 FAILED/255, 2 FAILED/1. The affected set (marker .done AND receipt status not OK) is exactly 47 - matching the reported count, arrived at independently. 30 + 47 + 2 = 79.
VERDICT: all 47 pass every one of the six reconciliation criteria under my own derivation. Zero problems were raised across the 47 by my checker.

TOTALS ACROSS THE 47: 11,241 assembled contigs, of which 4,763 are >= 1 kb (measured sequence length, not header annotation); 236,934,939 bp total. Every one of the 11,241 contigs received a definite call - 10,353 chromosome, 888 plasmid, 0 unknown. Contig reconciliation was perfect for all 47 (parsed/assembled 256/256, 346/346, 68/68, ... - contigs_parsed == contigs_assembled in every case), in both directions and against the output FASTAs, with per-contig length agreement.

CROSS-CHECK RESULT: 0 disagreements out of 11,241 contigs between my FASTA-membership derivation and the frozen parse_mobsuite, and 0 disagreements between my derivation and the contig_report molecule_type column read independently. No isolate produced a ParseError under either path. The agreement is between genuinely different data sources (per-record FASTA membership in chromosome.fasta / plasmid_*.fasta versus a column in a TSV), not a shared code path.

ROOT-CAUSE CORROBORATION (uniform across all 47, verified isolate by isolate): the mob_recon output and the .done marker were written by an earlier successful attempt and their mtimes precede the start_utc of the failing receipt in 47/47 cases; the failing attempt lasted 1-3 seconds and its log ends 'mob_suite.mob_recon ERROR: Error output directory exists, please specify a new directory or use --force to overwrite' in 47/47 cases. mob_recon aborts at that check BEFORE opening the output directory, so the failing attempt cannot have altered the evidence - it only clobbered the receipt JSON. This is a receipt-provenance defect, not a tool failure, and it is categorically different from the exit_code=1 pandas crash seen in the 2 genuine failures.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: both genuine failures leave residual output that the frozen parser parses without raising (115 and 82 contigs, 0 unknown). Trusting 'the output parses' alone would have wrongly recovered both. They are excluded by the marker gate, and independently by my required-file and leftover-__tmp checks. They must remain FAILED.

POSITIVE CONTROL: I ran the identical checker over the 30 mobsuite units that already carried status=OK (6,930 contigs). 0 problems, 0 cross-check diffs - confirming the checker does not merely pass whatever it is shown, and that the 47 are indistinguishable in output quality from units that were never disputed.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: no P1.11 truth artefact, reference genome, PAF, assembly report, GBFF or truth_hold path was opened, and none was created or fetched. No prediction score, truth label, expected class distribution or downstream performance quantity was consulted. The chromosome/plasmid counts reported here are tool outputs being audited for structural integrity, not accuracy measurements.

HOST HYGIENE: the host was treated as read-only. My only writes were /tmp/vv_indep_check.py and /tmp/vv_*.txt|json scratch files, all of which I removed. Pre-existing /tmp/vv_* files from earlier sessions were left untouched.

INTERPRETING n_pass / n_fail: n_examined 49 = the 47 affected isolates plus the 2 genuine-failure controls. n_pass 47 = all 47 affected isolates qualify as RECOVERED_OK. n_fail 2 = the two .failed controls, which correctly do NOT recover; they are not part of the 47 and their non-recovery is the expected and desired outcome. The ALL_PASS verdict refers to the 47.

isolates.reason: GENUINE FAILURE, NOT RECOVERED. Terminal marker is .failed (single marker), receipt status=FAILED exit_code=1 - a real non-zero tool exit, not the 255 read-only-directory clobber signature. The log ends in a mob_recon traceback: pandas ValueError 'No objects to concatenate' raised inside the aggregation stage, i.e. the run aborted mid-pipeline. Residual output DOES exist and is superficially convincing: mob/contig_report.txt has 115 rows covering all 115 assembly contigs (107 chromosome, 8 plasmid), chromosome.fasta and 2 plasmid FASTAs are present, and the frozen parse_mobsuite parses it without raising. That is precisely the trap the rule guards against. Under my own checks it also fails independently of the marker: biomarkers.blast.txt is absent, and the mob/__tmp working directory was left behind (contig_blast_results.txt, fixed.input.fasta and BLAST index files still in place), both signatures of a run that never reached cleanup. Per the reconciliation rule a unit with a .failed marker is NEVER recovered even if residual output parses - this isolate must remain FAILED regardless.
